title: ADAPT: Hybrid Prompt Optimization for LLM Feature Visualization
claim: A hybrid method seeds diverse candidates with a beam search, then refines them in a gradient-guided mutation loop.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right, dashed loops with color-coded token bars
description: The crop shows two stacked horizontal bands, probably the middle of a wider diagram. The top band is yellow and labeled 'Beam Search loop'. Dark pill-shaped sequences on the left feed into red, green and blue horizontal bars, which are the initial groups. Each bar expands into six sampled candidates (the k2 tokens per beam sequence), and the candidates go through a white 'Evaluation' box. The best candidates per group are kept, and a return arrow closes the loop. The lower band is light blue and titled 'Main Loop', with the note 'repeat for n_iterations'. Ranked bars numbered 1–7 pass through a 'Gradient Estimate' box. That box produces k1*k2 candidates, each with a darker mutated token segment, and these go to a second 'Evaluation' box. The selected set is outlined in red dashes, and faded bars fill the excess slots. Color encodes group identity, and dotted lines show the fan-out and fan-in.
caption: Diagram for ADAPT.
abstract: Understanding what features are encoded by learned directions in LLM activation space requires identifying inputs that strongly activate them. Feature visualization, which optimizes inputs to maximally activate a target direction, offers an alternative to costly dataset search approaches, but remains underexplored for LLMs due to the discrete nature of text. Furthermore, existing prompt optimization techniques are poorly suited to this domain, which is highly prone to local minima. To overcome these limitations, we introduce ADAPT, a hybrid method combining beam search initialization with adaptive gradient-guided mutation, designed around these failure modes. We evaluate on Sparse Autoencoder latents from Gemma 2 2B, proposing metrics grounded in dataset activation statistics to enable rigorous comparison, and show that ADAPT consistently outperforms prior methods across layers and latent types. Our results establish that feature visualization for LLMs is tractable, but requires design assumptions tailored to the domain.
